text: A feedback-channel setting (sound on/off and volume for the Focus chime and the idle warning, plus 'notify me when a cycle ends' for when the page is hidden) to replace the missing haptics on iOS
evidence: Focus plays a fixed-volume oscillator chime (js/modules/focus.js:893-905) with no on/off or volume setting anywhere, and only the idle warning/auto-end push a notification that becomes a device alert (focus.js:522-532); a cycle or break ending only chimes and toasts (focus.js:569-590).
note: You could turn the Focus chime on or off, set its loudness, and get a phone alert when a work cycle or break ends while the app is in the background.

text: Implement the ARIA tabs pattern once in KOS.ui.tabs (roving tabindex, arrows, aria-controls/tabpanel), or move view switchers to aria-current buttons
evidence: KOS.ui.tabs gives the workspace variant role=tablist/tab and aria-selected and the primary nav aria-current (js/core/ui.js:538-558), but there is no roving tabindex, no arrow/Home/End key handler and no aria-controls/tabpanel anywhere in ui.js (the scroller's keepRole branch at ui.js:744-758 defers keys to the tablist, which has none).
note: Keyboard and screen-reader users could move between a page's tabs with the arrow keys and hear which section each tab shows, as in standard apps.

text: A 'chip ink' token per role for Dawn and dark themes, with an automated contrast gate over chips and buttons in every shipped theme
evidence: css/tokens.css has per-surface ink tokens (--on-accent, --alarm-ink, --amber-ink, lines 104 and 1320-1321) and chip washes (1404-1410), but no chip-ink token per role, and no tool or smoke measures text contrast across themes (the only contrast maths is smoke108's colour helper, line 236; a8a8 grep for wcag/luminance found nothing else).
note: Coloured labels and buttons would stay easy to read in the light theme and every shop theme, with an automatic check that catches any that become faint.

text: Wardrobe redesign that shows only kinds you own
evidence: The Wardrobe (js/modules/governor-ui.js:1541-1632, 40c/SC-37) builds one cell only for kinds you own something of and lists every kind you own none of as a single 'Not owned yet:' line of shop links.
note: Already there: the Wardrobe shows only the kinds of item you own, with the rest as one line of links to the shop.

text: A refund or return window for shop items
evidence: KOS.governor.buy (js/core/governor.js:637-649) spends gold and records ownership with no undo or return path; the shop asks a confirm before buying instead of a timed Undo (js/modules/governor-ui.js:1043-1050), and the only refund is the one-off correction for retired themes (governor.js:209-218).
note: You could change your mind about a shop item for a short while after buying it and get your gold back.

text: Session Log rows for Code, Japanese, Mind and Creatives with their own details
evidence: The Session Log's activityInfo has its own cases for code, ja, mind and creatives entries with a label, title by kind and details read from their metrics (js/modules/governor-ui.js:169-195, marked AG-19).
note: Already there: the Session Log names Code, Japanese, Mind and Creatives work properly with what was done in each.

text: Lazy content loading: a per-subject/unit content manifest behind KOS.content.get, loading files on first open and a prebuilt search index
evidence: Content now loads on first use per subject bundle (index.html <template data-lazy="content-compsci|maths|it|code"> lines 328-425, js/core/lazy.js with the generated js/data/lazy-index.js stubs, invariant 168), but bundles are whole subjects, not units, and there is no prebuilt search index: search reads notes text only once a topic's content happens to be loaded (js/core/searchmore.js:215-230).
note: Search would find words inside every topic's notes straight away, even for subjects you have not opened yet this visit, and opening a subject would load a little faster.

text: A view lifecycle in KOS.show (onLeave/AbortController, a render token for async callbacks, a view-declared 'holds draft' flag replacing TASK_VIEWS) with focus restoration on rerender
evidence: js/core/redraw.js gives every render a lifecycle record with KOS.view.onDispose, an AbortController signal() and a render token() (lines 34-38, 176-192), a page-declared KOS.view.hold/guard for unsaved work (223-225, router.js:264, 369), and restores scroll, focus and caret on a redraw (297-346); a fixed TASK list of task pages still exists beside hold() (redraw.js:101).
note: Already there: leaving or redrawing a page cleans up its background work and keeps your place, focus and unsaved typing.

text: A small memo layer keyed on a store revision for readiness, code unit state, calendar derived items, srs.allCards and badge values
evidence: The store has a change counter (KOS.store.epoch) and exam readiness is memoised on it (js/core/exams.js:708-724), and badges cache their ledger walk (js/core/achievements.js:120-195), but srs.allCards (js/core/srs.js:450-461), Code unit state and the calendar's derived items are recomputed on every call and nothing else reads epoch; there is no shared memo layer.
note: Busy pages such as Home, Review and the Calendar would open and redraw faster, because the app would stop working out the same answers over and over.

text: Extract a shared lesson reader and checks-sync helper before the next study space
evidence: Each space carries its own copy of the paged lesson reader and the evidence-to-checks sync: markPage/syncChecks are re-implemented in js/core/code.js:231, ja.js:112/150, mind.js:96/398 and creatives.js:107/284, and the pager is rebuilt per space (js/modules/mindtopic.js:266-290 'the pager as Code's and Japanese's'); no shared reader or checks helper exists in js/core/ui.js.
note: Nothing changes on screen, but the next study space would be quicker to build and the four existing ones would behave the same way when reading lessons.

text: Split hub.js (home, topic page, backup, search listbox), aitools.js (per-domain tool registration) and governor-ui.js (stage, edit seat, shop, wardrobe)
evidence: hub.js is already split (its header says its pages are home.js, subject.js, topic.js, dataview.js and searchui.js, W8 AP-09; hub.js is now 829 lines), but js/core/aitools.js is still one 3,865-line file of 143 def() tools and js/modules/governor-ui.js still holds the Stage, Edit seat, Shop, Wardrobe and Session Log in 1,930 lines (sections at 322, 732, 956, 1485, 1694).
note: Nothing changes on screen; the Assistant's tools and the Governor pages would be easier and safer to change later.

text: Move the CLAUDE.md release diary to docs/RELEASES.md and split the invariants per domain
evidence: docs/RELEASES.md holds every release newest first and CLAUDE.md keeps only the latest-release line; the invariants live one file per domain in docs/invariants/ (core, exams, ink-files, media, productivity, spaces, study, sync, ui .md) with a one-line index in CLAUDE.md.
note: Already there: the release history and the app's rules are kept in their own tidy documents.

text: A single registry of persisted stores that drives snapshotFull/importFull, the coverage card and a smoke check
evidence: js/core/stores.js is one registry of every IndexedDB store with its backup key, and it drives Backup & Restore's coverage card (js/modules/dataview.js:193-197), Reset everything (dataview.js:329), Storage (js/modules/storage.js:176) and smoke134's unlisted-database check; but snapshotFull and importFull in js/core/store.js (e.g. 1395-1470) still list each part by hand instead of reading the registry.
note: A new kind of saved data could never be left out of your backup file or its restore by mistake, because the backup would follow the same list the Backup page shows.

text: Help & Guide generated from per-view help entries registered next to each view
evidence: Help & Guide is one hand-written SECTIONS array in js/modules/help.js (from line 10) and no view registers its own help entry (no KOS.help.* or per-view help registration found in js/).
note: The Help & Guide would always describe every page as it really is now, because each page would carry its own help text.

text: A 'state replaced' event that every in-memory cache (HUD, files index, theme, ink index) subscribes to
evidence: KOS.store.replaceState (js/core/store.js:1688-1696) fires no event; instead the restore page calls each cache by hand in afterRestore (cosmetics, HUD, rail counters, Files index, ink index, kept places; js/modules/dataview.js:274-286, AA-17), and the cloud pull's replace (js/core/cloudsync.js:775-799) goes through the change bus's rerender rather than a shared 'state replaced' signal.
note: After a restore or a cloud copy lands, every part of the screen (your profile card, theme, files list, handwriting) would update at once, with no stale bits left until a reload.

text: A single runner-status model shared by tasks, listings, retrieval and capstones (booting / ready / busy / failed) so timeouts during boot never reach the learner as code errors.
evidence: js/core/coderun.js has two separate status notions, the full runtime's absent/offline/downloading/ready/failed (lines 89-95) and the light runner's loading/ready status() (243-246), but a runtime boot that runs past its watchdog still comes back as an ordinary 'timeout' error (coderun.js:132-137) that the task, listing and editor views render as 'Did not finish — is there a loop…' (js/core/codeui.js:253-257, js/modules/code.js:725-767); there is no one booting/ready/busy/failed model shared by every surface.
note: While the code runner is still starting up you would see a clear 'getting ready' message, never a false message that your own code got stuck.

text: Language-aware task layout (console, method, SQL, Rider command) instead of one console template.
evidence: The task page (js/modules/code.js:602-695) is one template, always a stdin box, Output/Tests/Problems and 'Run tries your code with the input above', whatever the task is; only words change for method tasks ('Call'/'Returns', code.js:704-711, 835-837) and SQL only changes the highlighter and answer compare (js/modules/codetopic.js:569-606).
note: Each kind of coding task (a whole program, a single method, a database query, a Rider command) would get a screen shaped for it, without irrelevant boxes such as a keyboard input field for a query.

text: Code in global search: tasks, capstones, Rider projects and lessons as their own group.
evidence: Global search has a 'Code projects and tasks' group of capstones, Rider projects and tasks (js/core/searchmore.js:103-141, CO-38) and Code lessons as their own 'Code lessons' group (js/core/search.js:67-79).
note: Already there: searching finds Code lessons, tasks, capstones and Rider projects in their own groups.

text: One shared editor scaffold for all four vaults (score, cover, progress, bump, delete) so modules only add their own sections.
evidence: js/modules/medview.js already shares the frame and tails of every vault editor: editorModal, editorSection, editorTabs, editorBanner, editorActions with bump and delete, coverPositionControl, progressField, saveEntry and deleteEntry (lines 650-1290); but each vault still builds its own status, score, progress and cover inputs and its own save() (e.g. js/modules/anime.js:177-214, with the same done in books.js, vn.js and games.js).
note: The four Collection editors would handle score, cover, progress and delete the same way, so a fix or improvement in one reaches all four.

text: A 'unchanged' count in bulkUpsert results and a since-last-sync summary on Sync & Import.
evidence: bulkUpsert already returns an 'unchanged' count (js/core/mediadb.js:1138-1146, 1309-1316) and Sync & Import words it as 'N already up to date' after a pull (js/modules/mediasync.js:55-61, CL-32), but the page keeps only the last sync time and the imported total (stampFacts, mediasync.js:157-172); no summary of what changed since the last sync is stored or shown later.
note: Sync & Import would tell you what the last sync actually changed (added, updated, removed) even when you come back to the page later.

text: Purchase history view for the Wishlist (date, paid, vault link) separate from the buy queue.
evidence: The Wishlist has its own Purchased tab apart from Want to buy / Waiting for release (js/modules/wishlist.js:59, 753-757), whose rows show a 'bought <month>' chip, the price paid and a '⇄ Collection' link to the vault entry (wishlist.js:1017-1066), plus a monthly 'Purchase history' spend chart from budget.history (wishlist.js:805); only the day of purchase is not shown (month only).
note: Already there: the Wishlist keeps bought items on their own Purchased tab with when, how much and a link to the Collection entry.

text: An IT depth contract and smoke (like smoke65/66) for F201 and F206: worked levels-of-response answers, 6+ exam items, 10 quiz questions per leaf
evidence: F201 has a depth contract in tools/smoke156.test.js (paged notes, at least four OCR-style worked cards a leaf with a 6/9-mark levels-of-response answer, 12+ flashcards, 8+ quiz questions), set lower than the 6 exam items and 10 quiz questions asked; F206 (js/data/content/it-f206.js) has no depth smoke at all (it appears only in smoke58/138/154 for titles and unit state).
note: The IT units you still have to sit (F201 and the F206 project) would be held to the same depth as Computer Science, with enough exam-style answers and quiz questions on every topic.

text: A content lint in the smoke gate: validate_content, near-duplicate flashcards, quiz answer-position balance, duplicate exam src per leaf, markdown inside steps[].m
evidence: tools/smoke116.test.js already gates near-duplicate cards (B), answer positions (C), mark sums (D), callout kinds (E), duplicate ids and sources (F, G) and validate_content errors (H); nothing checks for markdown inside a worked step's text (steps[].m).
note: Most of this check is already in the test gate. The only part missing is a check for stray markdown inside worked-answer steps.

text: A content gate in the smoke suite: answer-position balance, near-duplicate flashcards, worked step marks summing to src marks, one exam item per past-paper question, validate_content clean.
evidence: tools/smoke116.test.js: B near-duplicate cards, C answer positions, D worked step marks sum to src marks, G duplicate sources within a leaf, H validate_content clean; it runs in the gate.
note: Already built: every subject's content goes through these checks in the test gate.

text: Open a notes diagram's lab in place (dialog or side pane) instead of navigating away.
evidence: Labs already open inside the notes: the {lab: id} fill-in embeds the lab at the reading width (js/core/fillins.js:25, :438 KOS.sims.embed) and the topic page embeds a leaf's sim (js/modules/topic.js:816); 'Open full page' is optional (js/labs/sims.js:141).
note: Already built: a diagram's lab opens in the notes themselves, with a button for the full page if you want it.

text: Deepen the thin core leaves (8.4, 8.1, 6.1, 6.2, 4.3, 7.2, 8.6) to the 4.1/M7.x depth with figures
evidence: Measured from KOS_CONTENT: 8.4, 8.1 and 6.2 have 6 note blocks, no pages and about 3–4k characters; 6.1, 4.3, 7.2, 8.6 have 10–11 blocks and 2 pages; 4.1 has 102 blocks, 6 pages, 31 worked examples and 85k characters. 4.3 has no figure.
note: Seven Maths topics are still short (about a twentieth of 4.1's notes). Writing them up to 4.1's depth, with diagrams, is a content job of a few sessions.

text: Regenerate the Maths spec text from a clean source (spec PDF re-extraction with fraction/superscript handling) and short S/M titles
evidence: W6 (32217b8, CM-01/CM-07/CM-28) re-typed the Maths spec from the Edexcel 9MA0 PDF (tools/maths_spec.py, gen_data.py --maths-spec) with maths as $…$, and gave Statistics and Mechanics short titles.
note: Already built: the Maths spec text was redone from the PDF with proper maths and short titles.

text: A content lint in validate_content for Maths: duplicate cards across base/bank, worked mark sums, label-only whys, callout kinds, two-option items, stem dependencies
evidence: smoke116 covers duplicate cards across base and bank (B), worked mark sums (D) and callout kinds (E); W6 fixed the two-option items and thin explanations once (32217b8), but no check stops a label-only 'why', a two-option item or a stem that leans on another from coming back.
note: Most of it is in the test gate. Missing: checks that would stop one-word explanations, two-option questions or questions that depend on another from creeping back in.

text: Fork staleness: store the shipped hash in a fork and offer 'the shipped notes changed — compare/reset'
evidence: W6 CM-04 (32217b8): a fork remembers its shipped version and says when the curriculum moved (new version, + my additions, keep mine); KOS.edits.stale (js/core/edits.js:324).
note: Already built: if you edited a topic and the shipped notes later change, the app tells you and lets you compare or keep yours.

text: A Portfolio view per track with a lightbox and export/share of a chosen piece.
evidence: The Portfolio page exists (js/modules/creatives.js:607 portfolioPage): one grid of every promoted piece, opening the piece's own page. There is no per-track view, no lightbox and no export or share of a piece.
note: You have a Portfolio grid already. Missing: a view per track, a full-screen viewer to flick through pieces, and a way to export or share one.

text: Attach saved Practice Log pieces to project milestones instead of bare ticks.
evidence: CR-20: a project milestone takes a piece already in the Practice Log or a new one (js/modules/creatives.js:650 attachDialog, 'Add your work'); js/core/creatives.js:28 'every milestone has a saved work attached'.
note: Already built: you attach a Practice Log piece to a milestone instead of just ticking it.

text: A phone composition for the sketchbook and Writing Desk on iPad portrait (toolbar-first, side panel as a drawer).
evidence: At 860px and below the sketchbook's side panel just stacks under the canvas (css/views/creatives.css:355-362, .k-crs-side position static); there is no toolbar-first layout or drawer for iPad portrait.
note: On iPad portrait the sketchbook and Writing Desk side panel drops below the page. This would make it a slide-out drawer with the tools on top.

text: Move the state document (or its big parts: srs, sessions, facets) from localStorage to IndexedDB with per-record writes and cross-tab coordination (BroadcastChannel or Web Locks).
evidence: The state document is still one localStorage document; it is mirrored to IndexedDB (kurenai-os-statemirror, js/core/store.js:506-536), which becomes the primary only when localStorage is full, and tabs coordinate with Web Locks (kos-state-write, invariant 33c). No per-record writes.
note: Your data already has an IndexedDB copy and tabs already take turns writing. Moving the big parts into IndexedDB for good, with small per-record saves, is a large engine change.

text: Replace per-device counter ids for assignments, reminders and events with random string ids, as Money, Routines and Exams already use, retiring rekeyCollisions.
evidence: Assignments still number ids per device (js/core/assignments.js:189 rec.id = s.nextId++; reminders.js:54 nextId) and cloudmerge.js:346 rekeyCollisions still re-keys clashes.
note: Assignments, reminders and events still use counting ids that can clash between devices (the app repairs clashes). Random ids like Money's would remove the repair step.

text: Make provider sync state-consistent: pull and push the cloud state around each leased cycle, and keep pending provider adds in synced state so any device recognises them.
evidence: A server lease makes one device sync a provider at a time (js/core/ext.js:297-323, DI-19) and deletions are a synced queue (state.ext.deletes); the cycle does not pull and push the cloud state around itself, and pending provider adds are not in synced state.
note: Only one device syncs Google or Todoist at a time already. Missing: syncing your app data just before and after each provider sync, so a second device never re-adds something.

text: Use a monotonic version column (bigserial) as the replication cursor for every kos_* table.
evidence: Replication still pages by updated_at; js/core/sidesync.js:13-17,77 works round late commits by asking from two minutes before the cursor. No kos_* table has a bigserial version column.
note: Sync currently re-reads a two-minute overlap to avoid missing rows. A proper version number per table would make that exact. Needs a database migration.

text: Audit every view for sub-objects of KOS.store.state captured at render and written later (stale after replaceState); with redraws held on task pages a stale page lives longer.
evidence: No audit has been done; redraw.js holds task pages behind a Refresh chip (invariant 165), which makes a page that captured a state sub-object at render live longer, as the idea warns.
note: A code audit for pages that keep an old copy of your data and save it back later. Not started.

text: A single store registry (name, namespace suffix, backup, restore semantics, reset, replication, status) that store.js, reset, Storage and the backup page all read, with a smoke asserting every indexedDB.open is registered.
evidence: js/core/stores.js is the one store registry (invariant 7): Backup & Restore and Reset everything read it, and smoke134 U fails when the app opens a database the table does not list.
note: Already built.

text: Auto-detect page corners in Scan pages
evidence: js/core/filescan.js:6 'nothing detects edges': each shot gets four corner handles you drag onto the page.
note: Scan pages makes you drag the four corners yourself. This would find them for you.

text: A proper 'paused' model for timed papers that matches the hall rule and reload
evidence: Timed papers: Pause hides the paper; with Rest breaks off the clock keeps running as in the hall (EX-32, js/modules/exampaperview.js:41-46); a reload comes back running and says so once (EX-42, :330-333).
note: Already built.

text: Sample data that never migrates into real records, with a one-tap remove
evidence: The sample account is its own namespace (js/core/sample.js; KOS.dataMode), never the real one, with sync off; one switch in Settings goes back to your data (js/modules/governor-ui.js:521-534).
note: Already built: the sample data lives in a separate account and one tap takes you back to yours.

text: Measure Collection goals from the media activity journal so they can repeat weekly/monthly (completions, episodes, chapters per period)
evidence: js/core/goals-collection.js measures Collection goals from each title's activity journal per period, so they repeat weekly or monthly (:9-33, REPEAT :63).
